kept.excerpt: The Senate seat at stake in this year’s election demands someone willing and prepared to address the issues Floridians actually live with: housing costs, insurance, health care, wages, child care, election integrity and government accountability. By that measure, The Miami Times endorses candidate Angie Nixon.
kept.relevance: This endorsement, dated at the cutoff, documents editorial support for Nixon and the economic issues emphasized in her candidacy.

kept.excerpt: Two Democrats are looking to unseat U.S. Sen. Ashley Moody, R-Florida, in November, but they have to get through the primary race first. State Rep. Angie Nixon, D-Jacksonville, is a progressive lawmaker. Alex Vindman is a retired U.S. Army lieutenant colonel.
kept.relevance: This recent local-news preview confirms the Nixon–Vindman primary contest remained active shortly before the cutoff.

kept.excerpt: Today, Common Defense, a leading national grassroots organization of veterans and military families, announced it is endorsing State Representative Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate in Florida. Rep. Nixon’s endorsements also include Congressman Maxwell Frost, Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley, Congresswoman Rashida Tlaib, Congresswoman Ilhan Omar, civil rights attorney Ben Crump, former Ohio State Senator Nina Turner, former Congressman Al Lawson, and former Congressman Jamaal Bowman.
kept.publisher: Angie Nixon for U.S. Senate — campaign press release
kept.relevance: This dated campaign statement identifies Nixon’s coalition and endorsements, while its partisan provenance should be considered when evaluating claims of momentum.

kept.excerpt: There’s been little public polling between the two Democrats as the primary nears. A big point of contention is that Vindman has avoided a debate with Nixon, much to her disappointment. One of Vindman’s most remarkable feats as a candidate to date has been his ability to raise money — more than $19 million since getting into the race in January, more than anyone else in the contest.
kept.relevance: This preview establishes sparse primary polling, the debate dispute, and Vindman’s fundraising strength without assuming those advantages determine primary votes.

kept.excerpt: The poll shows Moody up over Nixon, 50%-42%. Moody leads Vindman, 50%-40%. Vindman has reported raising $16.7 million. Nixon has reported raising a little more than $625,000, with approximately $118,000 cash on hand at the end of June.
kept.relevance: The UNF general-election matchups inform electability arguments, and the financial figures document the resource gap; these are not Democratic-primary voting-intention results.

kept.excerpt: The campaign was asked about internal polling in the Primary race, but did not provide even a topline during the availability. A Change Research poll released Thursday sheds some light though, showing Vindman up 34% to 24%, with 41% of Democrats undecided.
kept.relevance: This contemporaneous primary poll gives a direct measure of the contest, with Vindman leading Nixon but a large undecided share limiting confidence.

kept.excerpt: The Florida Division of Elections calendar lists Primary Election Day as August 18, 2026. It lists mandatory early voting for August 8–15, 2026, and the voter-registration deadline as July 20, 2026.
kept.publisher: Florida Department of State, Division of Elections
kept.relevance: The official calendar establishes the scheduled primary date and shows that the experiment cutoff falls during the mandatory early-voting period.

search_notes: Frozen cutoff: 2026-08-14, inclusive. Publication dates were checked against dated source text returned by web_search; the official calendar uses its dated 2025-02-04 revision. The Miami Times item displays an August 14 update date, corroborated by its dated endorsements roundup. web_fetch failed because of a provider-configuration error, and the requested agent-reach fallback returned RATE_LIMITED, so this pack relies on indexed source text rather than independently fetched full pages. The July 16 Florida Politics excerpt is confined to the originally dated article body; an subsequently changed image caption was excluded. No later developments, primary results, prediction-market pages, odds, or market prices are included. The UNF matchups are general-election polling and must not be interpreted as primary support. Fundraising totals are reproduced as reported by contemporaneous publications and were not independently reconciled with FEC filings.
